lotl.label: What's Going On With the Leafs
lotl.body: Quiet can be revealing in September - especially in Toronto, where the noise usually starts well before the games do. The Maple Leafs have brought Nick Blankenburg in on a PTO, a small transaction on paper that reads like a loud hint about the blue line and the uncertain health of the defense corps. The club is in the deep offseason now, its season finished and its focus narrowed to camp battles, not box scores. That makes the prospect track matter: Steve Sullivan has praised Luke Haymes' growth and said Tinus Luc Koblar is pushing to stay in North America, while Gavin McKenna arrives with the burden and promise that only a No. 1 pick can carry. What matters next is simple - training camp opens the real fight for roster spots, and Blankenburg has just made himself part of it.

the_latest.headline: Report: Leafs sign Nick Blankenburg to PTO

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Jays
lotl.body: The Blue Jays have stopped playing like a team waiting for permission - they've started taking it. Brett Bateman and Alejandro Kirk powered a 7-3 win over the Orioles, a sharp, loud answer after a rough stretch, and it mattered because Toronto is sitting at 74-75, still within reach but with no margin for another limp week. Bateman's pop has changed the tone of the lineup; Kirk keeps supplying the hard contact that steadies a club built on hope and stubbornness. Even in a bullpen day, the Jays found enough arms to keep the game from slipping away - that says something about the bench strength, and something else about the urgency. What to watch now is whether this offense can keep forcing the issue and turn one good night into a real late-season push.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Raptors
lotl.body: The quiet has a charge to it in Toronto - the kind that usually means a roster is about to be rearranged. Collin Murray-Boyles is here to break stuff is the right headline, because the young forward's edge looks like the identity piece this team has been hunting, and the chatter around the Kawhi Leonard return only sharpens the stakes as camp approaches. There's no games to chase and no standings to recite; this is about construction now, not survival. The Raptors are trying to build a sturdier, nastier spine around a group that still feels unfinished, and Murray-Boyles is the sort of defender who can make that ambition look less abstract. Training camp will tell us whether the new shape holds - and whether Toronto finally has enough bite to stop being pushed around.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Commanders
lotl.body: The opening whistle is still hours away, but the hard edge of the Commanders' season is already showing - this is a team built to be judged by its receiver room and its protection up front. Washington elevated C/G Julian Good-Jones from the practice squad on the eve of the opener against Philadelphia, a small move that says plenty about the state of the line and the urgency around Jayden Daniels' first snaps back. The Commanders finished 2025 at 8-9, and that record hangs over every roster decision now. Terry McLaurin remains the gravestone marker in the passing game; Stefon Diggs is the new stress test, the man who must punish any defense that dares bracket McLaurin. Watch the line, watch Diggs, and watch whether Washington's offense can look organized from the first series onward.

article.title: Sunday's Skate
paragraphs: The Leafs have signed Nick Blankenburg to a PTO, a small but useful camp note as training preparations keep filling out. The Blue Jays are back in the good kind of rhythm, with Sportsnet noting a power surge over the Orioles and Bluebird Banter pointing to another win on a bullpen day.

The Raptors are still deep in offseason mode, with Collin Murray-Boyles getting a hard-edged introduction to the job ahead and Sportsnet framing Kawhi Leonard as a key piece in the season ahead. For the Commanders, the focus is already on Week 1, where the conversation centers on how Stefon Diggs can punish Philadelphia if the Eagles crowd Terry McLaurin again.
